claude_only.name: Which system of record holds the authoritative identifier for this task instance, and what is that identifier value?
Within what namespace is the identifier guaranteed unique, and is uniqueness global or scoped to one server?
Which additional business, group or external identifiers correlate this task across exchanging systems?
If the work repeats, is each occurrence separately identified or derived from one recurring definition?
Which reusable task definition or process model does this instance instantiate, and at which pinned version?
Where does the running instance deviate from its definition, and who authorised the deviation?
How are later changes to the definition propagated to instances that are already running?
Was this task planned in advance by a definition or added discretionarily during execution?
What controlled code classifies the kind of work this task represents?
Is the work to be performed by a human, by an automated agent or service, or by a combination?
Which taxonomy governs these codes, who may extend it, and how are local extensions marked?
Which priority scale is in force, in which direction does it run, and what does an absent value mean?
Is business impact recorded separately from scheduling urgency on this task?
How is the local priority mapped when exchanged with a system using a different scale, and what precision is lost?
Who may change a task's priority after creation, and is the change recorded with a reason?
At what level of actionability does this task exist: proposal, plan, or authorised order?
Which request, work order or higher-level authorisation caused this task to exist, and is it still valid?
What does the authorisation permit and forbid in terms of repetitions, period and named recipient?
Which party remains accountable for the outcome when execution is delegated to another person or to an automated agent?
What may an automated performer do without a human confirmation step, and how is that boundary enforced?
Which combinations of requester, performer and approver are prohibited on the same task?
Who may intervene to suspend, reassign or terminate the task, and on what stated grounds?
Which parties hold each role on this task: initiator, potential owners, actual owner, stakeholders, administrators and excluded owners?
What competence, qualification, licence or system capability must a performer hold to be eligible?
How is the potential performer set resolved: by literal party list, by group query, or by expression over task data?
Is an unassigned task valid, and what happens when the potential performer set resolves to empty?
What operation makes a party the actual owner, and may more than one party hold the task simultaneously?
Under what conditions may an owner release the task, and to which state does it return?
Who is permitted to receive a delegated or forwarded task, and does accountability transfer with it?
How is a performer's response to an assignment recorded when it differs from the task's own status?
What is the task's current state in the governed vocabulary, and when was that state entered?
Which states are terminal, and may a terminal task be reopened or must a successor task be created?
What reason and domain-specific business status qualify the coded state beyond the enumerated value?
How does the local state map onto each aligned external vocabulary, and which distinctions cannot be preserved?
What is blocking progress: missing input, missing authorisation, an unmet dependency, or a deliberate hold?
What exact condition must be satisfied for work to resume, and who is able to satisfy it?
How long may the task remain blocked before escalation or automatic termination applies?
What is captured for each state transition: prior state, new state, actor, reason and time?
Is the time a transition occurred recorded separately from the time the system observed or ingested it?
Is the transition history complete and tamper-evident, and how would a missing entry be detected?
Which transitions on subtasks are propagated to the parent task's history, and which stay local?
How is an unsuccessful ending classified: failed, rejected, cancelled, obsolete, or entered in error?
What fault or error payload is retained, and is it safe to disclose to the requester?
What compensating, retry or successor action follows, and does it reuse the same task identity?
Which time anchors are recorded: authored, planned start, due, actual start, actual end and last modified?
Are all time values expressed with seconds and an explicit offset, and how is an unknown local offset represented?
In which local time zone or civil calendar is a deadline meaningful for the performer?
Which clock or system prevails when two systems report different times for the same transition?
Which deadlines apply, latest start or latest completion, and are they contractual or advisory?
What escalation fires when a deadline passes, to whom is it directed, and how often does it repeat?
Does this work repeat on a rule, and how is each occurrence instantiated and closed?
When both an absolute due time and a duration are present, which one governs?
Which parent task, work order or project does this task belong to, and is that membership exclusive?
Are subtasks executed in parallel or in sequence, and are they created automatically or on demand?
What condition over subtask outcomes completes the parent, and how is the parent result assembled?
What dependency type links this task to another: finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, start-to-finish, or a plain dependency?
What lead or lag applies to the dependency, and in which duration units?
How are dependency cycles and dangling references detected and rejected?
How is a dependency on a task held in another system or organisation expressed and resolved?
Which plan or schedule version places this task, and is that reference pinned to a version?
How is variance between planned and actual timing measured and reported back to the plan?
When the plan and the task disagree about dates, which one is authoritative?
What typed inputs, parameters and attachments must be present before work can start?
Which input values are bound at creation and which are supplied during execution?
How are inputs validated against the task definition, and what happens when validation fails?
What entity does this task act upon, and for whose benefit is it performed?
What conditions must hold for the task to count as complete, and are they machine-checkable?
Who accepts, reviews or verifies the result, and is acceptance a separate step from completion?
Is partial or conditional completion permitted, and how is it represented without misreporting success?
What preconditions, safety rules or policy constraints must hold before and during execution?
Which resources, tools, systems or instruments are required, and are any reserved exclusively for this task?
Where must the work be performed, and is that location a hard constraint or advisory?
What outputs, artifacts or deliverables does the task produce, and is each individually identified?
How is each output linked to the task that generated it and to the inputs it was derived from?
Are outputs immutable once the task reaches a terminal state, or may they be superseded?
How is progress quantified, on what scale, and who is permitted to update it?
What effort or duration was estimated and what has actually been consumed, in which units?
How reliable is a self-reported progress figure, and what independent signal corroborates it?
Which agent actually performed each step, in which role, and on whose behalf did it act?
Which entities were used and which were generated, with start and end times for the activity?
Which plan or definition qualified the agent's association with this task?
What evidence must be captured to prove the work was performed as specified?
How is evidence integrity protected against later alteration?
What makes the captured evidence sufficient for audit, and who decides sufficiency?
Who may see the task, its inputs and its outputs, and does visibility follow role assignment on the task?
What confidentiality classification applies to the task, and does it differ from that of its attachments?
How is emergency or break-glass access authorised, recorded and afterwards reviewed?
Which task fields can carry personal data about performers or subjects, and are they minimised?
How long are the task record, its history and its attachments retained after closure, and under whose authority?
Is deletion logical or physical, and what tombstone remains for audit after erasure?
How does a legal hold or investigation suspend a scheduled deletion, and who lifts it?
Which external task vocabularies is this model aligned to, and at which versions?
Which fields and states survive a round trip to each aligned vocabulary without loss?
What evidence supports a conformance claim, and where is alignment only partial?
How are concurrent updates to the same task detected and resolved: sequence number, revision token, or last writer wins?
How are duplicate create or transition requests recognised and made idempotent?
How is out-of-order delivery of status updates detected and corrected?
What happens when an update arrives for a task that has already reached a terminal state?

grok_only.name: What is the authoritative master-system identifier for this Task instance, and which system assigns and guarantees it?
Which business identifiers, group or requisition identifiers, and governed global IRIs also denote this Task?
Does the identifier remain stable across list moves, versioning and system copies, or must a Dimension UUID or ULID be assigned as a persistent surrogate?
What title or summary and free-text description should a human or agent use to recognize this Task?
Which categories, tags or outlook-style labels classify this Task for queues and search?
Is the Task public, private or confidential, and what privacy rules follow from that class?
What type or code describes the work this Task involves, and from which coding system?
Is this Task a proposal, plan, order or other intent level, and is that intent immutable for this instance?
What priority applies, on which native scale, and how is it mapped to the Dimension canonical priority?
Who created or requested this Task, and may that party cancel it?
Who is currently responsible for managing execution, and is an owner still unidentified?
Which actors actually performed the Task, and in what function or role?
Which access-control rules depend on requester versus owner versus performer?
Who are the potential owners, who is the actual owner, and by what claim or nomination did ownership become actual?
Which people or groups are excluded from becoming potential or actual owner?
Who are the task stakeholders and business administrators, and which administrative operations may they perform?
What higher-level authorization or request created this Task, if any?
What object, request or resource is this Task acting on, and must subtasks be used if more than one resource is manipulated?
Who benefits from the Task, and is the Task asking that the action not occur?
What is the current native workflow status, from which source vocabulary, and what is the mapped canonical state?
What business-specific substate, if any, refines the workflow status?
Why is the Task in its current status, especially if held, failed, refused or deferred?
When did this status become true as an event, and when was that change observed or ingested?
If the Task is terminal, was it completed, failed, cancelled, rejected, skipped, exited or entered-in-error, and what evidence supports that path?
Is work blocked waiting on others or deferred, and what unblocks it?
Which lifecycle operations are legal from the current state for this actor, including claim, release, start, stop, suspend, resume, delegate, forward, complete, fail and cancel?
Which parent Task, project, work order or task list contains this Task, and is the containment strict?
Which child Tasks or checklist items decompose this Task, and what completion condition rolls them up?
Which related tasks, events, journals, plans or linked resources are associated, and with what relationship type?
If multiple people or subtasks are involved, what sequential, parallel or mixed routing pattern applies?
When should this Task start and be due, and in which time zone or offset?
When did execution actually start and end, when was the Task completed, and when were those facts observed or ingested?
Does the Task recur, and what reminder or VALARM triggers apply, including overdue behavior?
Where is this Task expected or observed to occur, including virtual locations?
What equipment or resources are required to perform the Task?
If a geographic point is recorded, what coordinates and datum identify that place?
Which named inputs must or may be present before the Task can complete, and which are missing?
Which named outputs or result were produced, and what error describes a failed action?
What fulfillment restrictions apply, what percent is complete, and which possible outcomes remain open?
Why does this Task need to be performed, as a code or referenced justification?
Who was associated with or attributed for each key Task change, and on whose behalf did they act?
What notes, comments, file attachments and renderings document work on this Task?
Is the recorded history complete enough to compute wait time, time in progress and time to completion, and where are the gaps?
Who may read, update, claim or administer this Task, and which confidentiality class or security labels apply?
How long is the Task and its attachments retained, and what deletion, anonymization or legal-hold exceptions apply?
Which external Task, to-do, human-task or action models is this instance aligned to, and which known conflicts remain unmapped?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
